dialogs.about: 아들과 집에서 비상 가방을 챙기며 이야기

lines.en: Mom, the news says a typhoon is coming.
I heard that too. Are the windows closed?
Yes, I closed them all this morning.
Good. Let's put water and food in this bag.
lines.ko: 좋아요. 이 가방에 물하고 음식을 넣어요.

lines.en: Mom, where is our town shelter?
The shelter is the school on the hill.
Will we evacuate if a flood comes?
Yes, we will evacuate early and stay safe.
lines.ko: 네, 일찍 대피해서 안전하게 있을 거예요.

lines.en: The earthquake last year made our lamp shake.
lines.ko: 작년 지진 때 우리 등이 흔들렸어요.

lines.en: Yes, but the damage was small then. Thank you.
lines.ko: 네, 그런데 그때 피해는 작았어요. 고마워요.

dialogs.about: 마을 회관에서 안내원에게 대피 안내를 듣다

lines.en: Good morning. Is this the safe shelter place?
Yes, Ma'am. This hall is our village shelter.
lines.ko: 네. 이 회관이 우리 마을 대피소예요.

lines.en: How do people evacuate during a big flood?
lines.ko: 큰 홍수 때 사람들은 어떻게 대피해요?

lines.en: We call everyone and walk up the hill road.
Was there much damage from the typhoon?
A landslide closed one road last autumn.
Oh dear. Did the ground shake here also?
A small earthquake shook the town two years ago.
lines.ko: 이 년 전에 작은 지진이 마을을 흔들었어요.

lines.en: Thank you for helping us understand this.
You are welcome. We will practice again next month.
lines.ko: 천만에요. 다음 달에 또 연습할 거예요.
